section_summary.extract_value: This paper evaluated the factorial and construct validity of a Standard Chinese translation of the BAS-2 in a sample of 191 women and 154 men from mainland China who were resident in Hong Kong. Confirmatory factor analysis supported a one-dimensional BAS-2 structure invariant across sex, and body appreciation scores showed good internal consistency and expected correlations with self-esteem and life satisfaction; in women only, scores were significantly correlated with weight discrepancy and BMI. The findings suggest the Standard Chinese BAS-2 is equivalent to the parent scale and useful for cross-cultural research.
section_summary.evidence_source: The present study examined the factorial and construct validity of a Standard Chinese translation of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS-2; Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015b). Participants were 191 women and 154 men from mainland China who were resident in Hong Kong at the time of recruitment. Results of confirmatory factor analysis indicated thatthe one-dimensional model ofthe BAS-2, in which all 10 items loaded onto the same factor, had adequate fit, and was invariant across sex. Body appreciation scores had good internal consistency and were significantly correlated with self-esteem and life satisfaction, and, in women, with weight discrepancy and body mass index.
